subproblem.title: Tilt-excess bounded by height with an L^1 mean-curvature term (Lemma A)
subproblem.statement: For n >= 1 and l >= 0 there is a constant C >= 0 (one may take C = 144) such that: if U is open, V is a rectifiable n-varifold in U with generalized mean curvature H in U, z in R^(n+l), r > 0, h >= 0, B_r(z) contained in U, T an n-dimensional subspace, and dist(x - z, T) <= h for every x in spt V cap B_r(z), then integral_{B_{r/2}(z)} |p_x - p_T|^2 dmu <= C r^-2 integral_{B_r(z)} dist(x - z, T)^2 dmu + C h integral_{B_r(z)} |H| dmu (Bochner integrals with respect to mu = V.weight; |.| Hilbert-Schmidt; p_x = V.tangentProj x; balls closed).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → ∃ C : ℝ, 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)), IsOpen U → ∀ (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (H : Amb n ℓ → Amb n ℓ), V.HasGeneralizedMeanCurvature H → ∀ (z : Amb n ℓ) (r h : ℝ), 0 < r → 0 ≤ h → closedBall z r ⊆ U → ∀ T : Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ), Module.finrank ℝ T = n → (∀ x ∈ V.support ∩ closedBall z r, infDist (x - z) (T : Set (Amb n ℓ)) ≤ h) → ∫ x in closedBall z (r / 2), hsNormSq (V.tangentProj x - T.starProjection) ∂V.weight ≤ C * (r ^ 2)⁻¹ * ∫ x in closedBall z r, infDist (x - z) (T : Set (Amb n ℓ)) ^ 2 ∂V.weight + C * h * ∫ x in closedBall z r, ‖H x‖ ∂V.weight
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Lemma A of the parent proof (the L^1 form of the computation proving Simon Ch. 5, Lemma 2.1), with a general cut-off so that the constant is an absolute number C (C = 144 when |phi'| <= 3).

Notation. mu := V.weight, spt V := V.support, p_x := V.tangentProj x, p_T := T.starProjection, |A| the Hilbert-Schmidt norm (|A|^2 = hsNormSq A = trace(A^* A)), ||A|| the operator norm (||A|| <= |A|), x' := p_{T^perp}(x - z), so |x'| = dist(x - z, T) = infDist (x - z) T.
Facts used. (T) [sibling allard52_tangent_ae] p is mu-a.e. strongly measurable, and for mu-a.e. x, p_x is the orthogonal projection onto an n-dimensional subspace. (F2) mu(K) < infinity for compact K in U (theta is integrable on M cap K); mu(R^(n+l) minus spt mu) = 0 and mu(R^(n+l) minus U) = 0, so mu-a.e. point lies in spt V.

1. Cut-off and constant. Fix phi in C^infinity(R, [0,1]) with phi = 1 on (-infinity, 1/2] and phi = 0 on [1, infinity) (for instance a mollified piecewise linear function, which can be chosen with |phi'| <= 3), let c_phi := sup|phi'| < infinity and C := max{16 c_phi^2, 4} (C = 144 if c_phi = 3). C is an absolute constant. Given z, r, h, T as in the statement put zeta(x) := phi(|x - z|/r). Since phi is constant near 0, zeta is C^infinity; 0 <= zeta <= 1, zeta = 1 on B_{r/2}(z), zeta = 0 outside the open ball B^o_r(z), and |grad zeta| <= c_phi / r.

2. Test field. X(x) := zeta(x)^2 x' = zeta(x)^2 p_{T^perp}(x - z). X is C^infinity, tsupport X is contained in B_r(z), which is a compact subset of U, so X is admissible in V.HasGeneralizedMeanCurvature H: integral div_M X dmu = -integral X.H dmu, where div_M X(x) = V.divM X x = trace(DX(x) o p_x). (X.H is integrable since H is in L^1_loc(mu) on U and X is bounded with compact support in U.)

3. Divergence. DX(x)v = zeta^2 p_{T^perp} v + 2 zeta (grad zeta . v) x'. At mu-a.e. x, p_x is the orthogonal projection onto an n-dimensional subspace (T); there trace(DX o p_x) = zeta^2 trace(p_{T^perp} p_x) + 2 zeta grad zeta . p_x x' (the trace of v -> (a . p_x v) b is a . p_x b). For two rank-n orthogonal projections, |p_x - p_T|^2 = trace((p_x - p_T)^2) = 2n - 2 trace(p_T p_x), so trace(p_{T^perp} p_x) = n - trace(p_T p_x) = (1/2)|p_x - p_T|^2 =: s(x); and p_T x' = 0 gives p_x x' = (p_x - p_T)x'. Hence div_M X = zeta^2 s + 2 zeta grad zeta . (p_x - p_T) x' for mu-a.e. x.

4. Integrability. All functions involved are bounded (|p_x - p_T|^2 <= (|p_x| + |p_T|)^2 <= 4n since p_x is 0 or a rank-n projection), mu-a.e. strongly measurable by (T), and vanish outside B_r(z), which has finite mu-measure by (F2). Hence they are mu-integrable, and the first variation identity becomes
 integral zeta^2 s dmu = -integral 2 zeta grad zeta . (p_x - p_T) x' dmu - integral zeta^2 x' . H dmu.

5. Absorption. |(p_x - p_T) x'| <= ||p_x - p_T|| |x'| <= |p_x - p_T| |x'| = sqrt(2s) |x'|, and with a := zeta sqrt(s), b := |grad zeta| |x'| we have 2 sqrt(2) a b <= a^2/2 + 4 b^2 (as (a/sqrt 2 - 2b)^2 >= 0). Hence |2 zeta grad zeta . (p_x - p_T)x'| <= (1/2) zeta^2 s + 4 |grad zeta|^2 |x'|^2, and |zeta^2 x'.H| <= zeta^2 |x'| |H|. So integral zeta^2 s <= (1/2) integral zeta^2 s + 4 integral |grad zeta|^2 |x'|^2 + integral zeta^2 |x'| |H|, and since integral zeta^2 s < infinity,
 integral zeta^2 s dmu <= 8 integral |grad zeta|^2 |x'|^2 dmu + 2 integral zeta^2 |x'| |H| dmu.

6. Conclusion. As zeta = 1 on B_{r/2}(z) and s >= 0, (1/2) integral_{B_{r/2}(z)} |p_x - p_T|^2 dmu <= integral zeta^2 s dmu. As |grad zeta|^2 <= c_phi^2 r^-2 and grad zeta, zeta vanish outside B_r(z), integral |grad zeta|^2 |x'|^2 dmu <= c_phi^2 r^-2 integral_{B_r(z)} dist(x - z, T)^2 dmu. mu-a.e. x in B_r(z) lies in spt V cap B_r(z) (F2) and therefore satisfies |x'| = dist(x - z, T) <= h by hypothesis, so integral zeta^2 |x'| |H| dmu <= h integral_{B_r(z)} |H| dmu. Therefore
 integral_{B_{r/2}(z)} |p_x - p_T|^2 dmu <= 16 c_phi^2 r^-2 integral_{B_r(z)} dist(x - z, T)^2 dmu + 4 h integral_{B_r(z)} |H| dmu <= C (r^2)^-1 integral_{B_r(z)} dist(x - z, T)^2 dmu + C h integral_{B_r(z)} |H| dmu.
 All integrals here are Bochner integrals of integrable functions: the left integrand by step 4, dist(x - z, T)^2 is continuous and bounded on the compact set B_r(z) of finite measure, and |H| is integrable on B_r(z) because H is in L^1_loc(mu) on U (V.HasGeneralizedMeanCurvature H) and B_r(z) is a compact subset of U. This is the asserted inequality with the constant C, which depends on nothing.
proof_key_steps: Cut-off zeta = phi(|x - z|/r) and test field X = zeta^2 p_{T^perp}(x - z)
div_M X = zeta^2 (1/2)|p_x - p_T|^2 + 2 zeta grad zeta . (p_x - p_T) x' at mu-a.e. x
First variation identity with bounded integrable terms
Absorb the cross term by AM-GM
Use zeta = 1 on B_{r/2}(z), |grad zeta| <= c/r, and |x'| <= h at mu-a.e. point of B_r(z)

audit.reason: The prose and type agree. The admissible cutoff field, projection trace identity and absorption estimate prove the inequality. Compact containment and local integrability justify the Bochner integrals; the common constant C = 144 suffices.
